description: we are interested in space and mars
summary: we built a game that help people to know about equipments in the space
details:
1. Our project is an interactive educational game and presentation about space exploration equipment (Spacesuit, Space Telescope, Opportunity Rover, and International Space Station). Players view real photos and clear definitions of each piece of equipment, then answer short quiz questions to test their knowledge and progress through the mission.

2.

  • Makes learning fun: Turns complex space science into an engaging, game-based experience instead of passive reading.
  • Visual memory: Connects real space photography with concise definitions so students remember how each tool works.
  • Self-assessment: Immediate short-answer questions help learners check their understanding right away.

3. Our goal is to inspire students to become curious about astronomy, space technology, and STEM fields by showing how real engineering tools help humanity explore planets and distant galaxies.

4.

  • Game Development (Hossam & Saad): Game-building and coding tools (such as Scratch, Power point ) to create the interactive quiz logic and scoring.
  • Visuals & Media (Miral): Image editing and design tools to select, format, and optimize high-resolution NASA and space photography.
  • Research & Presentation (Hamza & Abdulrahman): Scientific databases (NASA archives) and presentation software (HTML/PowerPoint slides) to structure accurate definitions and questions.
  • Hardware: Standard laptops and PCs used for coding, research, and testing.

5.

  • Storytelling & Roleplay: Equipment like the Opportunity Rover speaks in the first person ("I am the rover Opportunity...") to tell its real Mars mission story instead of dry textbook facts.
  • Gamified Learning: Combines visual cards, real-world definitions, and rapid-fire single-word quiz challenges in a dark, space-themed interface.

6.

  • Clarity & Simplicity: Keeping definitions short and questions focused on one-word or brief answers so players of all ages can play easily.
  • Scientific Accuracy: Verifying every fact, mission detail, and NASA photo before adding it to the game.
  • Teamwork & Role Division: Splitting responsibilities clearly between game development, visual design, and scientific research
